name: Sāmāyika (equanimity practice)
method_summary: For a fixed period (a muhūrta, 48 minutes) the practitioner renounces all harmful activity of mind, speech and body and sits (or stands) in equanimity, reciting the vow of sāmāyika, praising the Jinas, reflecting on the realities and cultivating friendliness toward all beings (Amitagati's Sāmāyikapāṭha), treating friend and foe, gain and loss alike. For the layman it is a disciplinary vow and a temporary taste of the ascetic life; for the ascetic it is lifelong conduct.
prerequisites: the small vows (for the lay vow)
duration: one muhūrta (48 minutes) per session, one or more times a day
signs_of_progress: equanimity toward the agreeable and disagreeable
steadiness of mind that supports meditation (YŚ 4.114)

warnings.text: Careless practice — wandering mind, improper posture, forgetting the time — is a transgression of the vow.

name: Pratikramaṇa (repentance, 'turning back')
method_summary: A liturgy of reviewing, confessing and repenting the faults of the day, night, fortnight, four months or year: the practitioner recites the Āvaśyaka formulas, names the kinds of harm done to beings, says 'micchāmi dukkaḍaṃ' (may my wrongdoing be fruitless), and asks and grants forgiveness to all beings; the yearly pratikramaṇa closes Paryuṣaṇa.
duration: morning and evening; fortnightly, four-monthly and yearly forms
notes: The Śvetāmbara forgiveness verse 'khāmemi savve jīvā, savve jīvā khamaṃtu me, mittī me savvabhūesu, veraṃ majjha na keṇaï' is recited (wording as commonly recited).

name: Kāyotsarga (abandonment of the body)
method_summary: Standing upright (or sitting) motionless with arms hanging, eyes on the tip of the nose or closed, indifferent to the body and to hardships, for a period measured by silent recitations (e.g. of the Logassa or Namaskāra) or breaths; part of every liturgy and a form of internal austerity; the Jinas are depicted in this posture.
duration: from a few breaths to long periods (ascetics)
signs_of_progress: loosening of identification with the body

name: The six essential duties
method_summary: Daily performance of sāmāyika, praise of the twenty-four Jinas, salutation of the teacher, pratikramaṇa, kāyotsarga and a vow of renunciation (pratyākhyāna); for Digambara householders also the six daily duties of worship, attendance on the teacher, study, restraint, austerity and giving.

name: Ālocanā (confession to the teacher)
method_summary: The practitioner discloses his faults to the teacher fully and without concealment or self-justification, as a child tells its mother, and accepts the expiation assigned.

warnings.text: Confession with concealment, or choosing a lenient teacher, is itself a fault (ten faults of confession in the ācāra texts, recalled).

name: Prāyaścitta (expiation)
method_summary: Correction of faults by nine (Śvetāmbara ten) graded means: confession, repentance, both, discrimination (giving up the faulty object), abandonment (kāyotsarga), austerity, reduction of seniority, exclusion and re-initiation, assigned by the ācārya.

name: Kṣamāpanā (asking and granting forgiveness)
method_summary: Asking forgiveness of all beings and granting it, individually and collectively, especially on the last day of Paryuṣaṇa, with the words 'micchāmi dukkaḍaṃ'.

name: Paryuṣaṇa and Daśalakṣaṇa
method_summary: The annual festival of the rains: eight days for Śvetāmbaras (with recitation of the Kalpa Sūtra, fasting, and the yearly pratikramaṇa and forgiveness on Saṃvatsarī), ten days for Digambaras, each devoted to one of the ten virtues (supreme forbearance …).

name: Proṣadhopavāsa / pauṣadha (holy-day fast and retreat)
method_summary: On the eighth and fourteenth days of the lunar fortnight the householder fasts and spends the day and night in the temple or hall as a temporary ascetic, in study, sāmāyika and meditation.

name: The great vows of the ascetic
method_summary: Lifelong, total abstention from violence, falsehood, stealing, sexual activity and possession, in thought, word and deed, by doing, causing and approving, supported by the twenty-five contemplations; Śvetāmbaras add not eating at night.

name: The small vows and lay vows
method_summary: The householder keeps the five vows partially — no intentional violence to mobile beings, no gross falsehood or theft, fidelity to one's spouse, limits on possessions — with three supplementary and four disciplinary vows.

name: The controls and carefulnesses
method_summary: Restraining mind, speech and body, and moving, speaking, begging, handling objects and excreting with constant care not to injure living beings — looking ahead while walking, sweeping with the broom (rajoharaṇa/picchī), speaking gently.

name: The eleven lay stages (pratimā)
method_summary: The householder progresses through eleven stages of renunciation, each adding a discipline — right view, vows, regular sāmāyika, holy-day fasts, not eating living food, not eating at night, celibacy, giving up business, giving up possessions, not approving household acts, not accepting food prepared for oneself — until close to ascetic life.

name: Not eating at night
method_summary: Taking no food or drink after sunset (and before sunrise), to avoid harming small beings that cannot be seen; a sixth vow for Śvetāmbara ascetics and a basic lay observance.

name: Giving (dāna) and sharing with ascetics
method_summary: Giving food, medicine, knowledge and fearlessness; above all offering pure food to wandering ascetics who arrive unannounced, with the proper manner, thing, giver and recipient.

name: Ahiṃsā (non-injury)
method_summary: Jain contribution: care not to injure any living being, including earth-, water-, fire-, air- and plant-bodied beings, through careful movement, filtering water, not eating at night, avoiding root vegetables and honey (lay rules vary), and above all through freedom from the passions, whose arising is itself violence.

name: Jain initiation (dīkṣā)
method_summary: The candidate, having received the teacher's permission (and, for Śvetāmbaras, the family's), renounces household life, plucks out the hair, receives the great vows and the ascetic's requisites (Śvetāmbara: white robes, broom, bowls, mouth-cloth; Digambara monks: nudity, peacock-feather whisk, water-gourd) and a new name.

name: Keśa-loca (plucking the hair)
method_summary: At initiation and periodically thereafter the ascetic plucks out the hair of head and face by hand, as endurance of pain and freedom from bodily care; one of the twenty-eight basic qualities of the Digambara monk.

warnings.text: Undertaken as austerity without attachment; done for show it is the 'poison' kind of performance (Yogabindu).

name: Silence (mauna)
method_summary: Periods of silence, and speech restrained to what is true, beneficial and necessary (the control of speech).

name: Tapas (austerity) — the twelvefold
method_summary: Jain contribution: six external austerities (fasting, eating less, limiting alms, giving up tasty food, lonely lodging, bodily hardship) and six internal (expiation, humility, service, study, abandonment, meditation), practised according to one's capacity to stop and shed karma.

warnings.text: Austerity is to be done 'according to one's capacity' (śaktitaḥ).
Austerity done for worldly or heavenly reward is 'poison' or 'venom'; only austerity with understanding and longing for release counts.
Austerity of the ignorant (bāla-tapas) binds divine rebirth, not liberation.

name: Fasting (anaśana)
method_summary: Abstaining from food for a fixed period — from one meal or one day to long fasts undertaken by some ascetics and laity — and, at life's end, the final fast (see prc:sallekhana).

warnings.text: To be undertaken according to capacity and without passion; fasting done for fame or reward binds rather than sheds karma.
Fasting must not disturb the mind: austerity that agitates is not meditation's support (cf. YŚ 4.114).

notes: Restricted: prolonged fasting — summary and the texts' warnings only; no durations or regimens recorded.

name: Eating less (ūnodarī)
method_summary: Eating less than one's fill, as external austerity.

name: Giving up tasty food
method_summary: Abstaining from one or more of the rich foods (ghee, milk, curd, oil, sweets, salt) for a period.

name: Kāyakleśa (bodily hardship)
method_summary: Enduring hardship in the body — difficult postures, exposure to sun and cold, staying awake — as external austerity.

warnings.text: Only according to capacity and without disturbing the mind; the aim is detachment from the body, not injury to it.

name: Āyambil (plain-food fast)
method_summary: A day with one meal of plain boiled grain or pulses without salt, oil, spices, milk or sweets, eaten once; repeated during the Navapada Olī.

name: Navapada Olī (Siddhacakra worship)
method_summary: Twice a year for nine days the practitioner worships the Siddhacakra yantra of the nine stations (Arhat, Siddha, Ācārya, Upādhyāya, Sādhu, right view, knowledge, conduct, austerity), keeps plain-food fasts and hears the story of Śrīpāla.

name: Vaiyāvṛttya (service)
method_summary: Serving teachers, ascetics, novices, the sick and the community with food, medicine, care and help — an internal austerity.

name: Vinaya (reverence)
method_summary: Reverence toward knowledge, right view, conduct and the worthy, expressed in respectful conduct toward teachers.

name: Svādhyāya (study)
method_summary: Jain contribution: fivefold study — reading and teaching, questioning, reflection, recitation and preaching — an internal austerity and a daily duty.

name: Vandana (salutation of the teacher and the Jina)
method_summary: Formal veneration of the teacher (guru-vandana) and of the Jina (caitya-vandana) with bows and recitations.

name: Anuprekṣā (the twelve reflections)
method_summary: Repeated contemplation of impermanence, the lack of refuge, the round of births, aloneness, the otherness of self and body, the body's impurity, inflow, stopping, shedding, the universe, the rarity of enlightenment and the well-taught dharma, producing detachment and fitness for meditation.
signs_of_progress: dread of saṃsāra and longing for release

name: The four attitudes (maitrī, pramoda, kāruṇya, mādhyasthya)
method_summary: Cultivating friendliness to all beings ('may no one do evil, may no one suffer, may the world be freed'), joy at the virtues of others, compassion for the afflicted, and impartiality toward the incorrigible; recited in the Sāmāyikapāṭha and used to support meditation.

equivalents.note: Same four attitudes as Yoga Sūtra 1.33 with different objects.

name: Dharma-dhyāna (virtuous meditation)
method_summary: Fixing the mind on one of four objects: the Jina's command (the realities as taught), the harm and misery of wrong ways, the fruition of karma, and the structure of the universe; supported by the reflections, the four attitudes and equanimity; also practised through the four objects (piṇḍastha …).
stage: guṇasthānas 4–7 (Digambara); up to 12 in some Śvetāmbara accounts
prerequisites: a qualified meditator and suitable place (Jñānārṇava)
duration: up to one muhūrta at a time

name: Śukla-dhyāna (pure meditation)
method_summary: Four stages: scripture-based meditation shifting among aspects, words and activities; fixed on one aspect without shifting (which yields omniscience); the omniscient's meditation in which only subtle activity remains; and the stopping of all activity before liberation.
prerequisites: knowledge of the Pūrvas (first two stages)

warnings.text: The tradition holds that the first two stages require the best bodily frame and knowledge of the lost Pūrvas, and so are not attainable in the present age in Bharata.

name: Piṇḍastha-dhyāna (embodied meditation)
method_summary: Meditation through the five concentrations: visualising the world as an ocean of milk with a lotus on which one sits; fire arising from 'arhaṃ' burning the lotus of the eight karmas and the body; wind scattering the ashes; rain washing them away; and seeing oneself as the pure, omniscient Siddha.

name: The five concentrations (pārthivī … tattvabhū)
method_summary: The earth, fire, wind, water and essential concentrations that make up embodied meditation (see prc:pindastha-dhyana).

name: Padastha-dhyāna (meditation on sacred words)
method_summary: Meditation on letters and mantras: the sixteen vowels on a lotus at the navel, the consonants on a lotus at the heart, the syllable 'arhaṃ', the five-line homage and its shorter forms, visualised and silently recited according to the teacher's instruction.

warnings.text: Mantras are to be meditated on for purification and liberation; using them to harm, attract or subjugate is evil meditation.

name: Rūpastha-dhyāna (meditation on the Arhat's form)
method_summary: Meditating on the Arhat seated in the assembly hall, radiant, free of passion, teaching all beings; or on his image.

warnings.text: One should not meditate on deities in passionate or fearsome forms, since one becomes like what one meditates on.

name: Rūpātīta-dhyāna (formless meditation)
method_summary: Meditating on the formless, bodiless Siddha of pure consciousness and bliss, and on one's own self as of that nature, until meditator and object are not experienced as two.

name: Bheda-vijñāna (discriminating self from non-self)
method_summary: Repeatedly discerning that the knowing self is other than body, karma, passions and thoughts — 'I am one, pure, made of perception and knowledge; nothing else, not even an atom, is mine' — and resting in self-experience; the core practice of the Adhyātma path.

warnings.text: Taking the ultimate standpoint alone while abandoning conduct is itself a wrong view (niścayābhāsa).

equivalents.note: Discrimination of seer and seen in Yoga; the Jain knower is an agent with modes.

name: Āsana (meditation postures)
method_summary: Jain contribution: Hemacandra lists the paryaṅka, vīra, vajra, lotus, bhadra, daṇḍa, utkaṭikā and godohikā seats and the standing kāyotsarga, allowing whichever keeps the mind steady; Haribhadra's balā view is the stage of steady posture.

name: Prāṇāyāma
method_summary: Jain contribution: Hemacandra and Śubhacandra describe filling, holding and expelling the breath, the five winds and the breath's four circles and omens, but declare that breath-control torments the mind and is not a means to liberation; Haribhadra gives prāṇāyāma an inner sense (expelling outer states, taking in inner ones).

warnings.text: Restraining the breath causes pain and the pain disturbs the mind; breath-control is not a means to liberation.
Those who pursue breath-control for powers fall into distress.

name: Kālajñāna (foreknowing the time of death)
method_summary: Reading signs in the breath, the body, shadows and dreams to foreknow the approach of death, so that one may prepare with equanimity and, if appropriate, undertake the final renunciation.

name: Entering another body (parapura-praveśa)
method_summary: Described by Hemacandra only as a wonder, reached (if at all) by long breath-practice; of no use for liberation.

warnings.text: It may not succeed even with great effort over a long time, and it is merely a marvel.

name: Sallekhanā / saṃthārā (the final fast)
method_summary: At the approach of death that cannot be averted (calamity, famine, old age, incurable illness), the practitioner, with the teacher's permission and under the care of attending ascetics, gradually gives up food and passions, forgives and asks forgiveness, and dies in equanimity reciting the homage to the five supreme beings.
stage: advanced; the culmination of the lay vows and of ascetic life

warnings.text: Only when death cannot be averted: calamity, famine, old age or incurable disease.
Vitiated by wishing to live, wishing to die, affection for friends, recalling pleasures and longing for future reward.
One who ends life by water, fire, poison or weapon under the sway of passion commits self-killing; only passionless thinning of the passions is sallekhanā.
To be undertaken with the teacher's permission, gradually, under attending ascetics, and abandoned faults of fear and attachment.

notes: Restricted: summary and the texts' own conditions and warnings only; no procedure, durations or stages recorded.

name: Recitation of the Namaskāra mantra
method_summary: Reciting the five-line homage (with the cūlikā among Śvetāmbaras) aloud, whispered or mentally, often on a rosary of 108 beads (the 108 qualities of the five supreme beings), at waking, before meals and journeys and at death; meditating on its shorter forms (a-si-ā-u-sā, arhaṃ, oṃ) by the teacher's instruction; the preparatory austerities (upadhāna) for learning it are prescribed in Śvetāmbara texts.

warnings.text: Mantra is for purification and liberation, not for harming or gaining power over others.

name: Ānupūrvī (permuted recitation)
method_summary: Reciting the five padas of the Namaskāra in the permuted orders printed in ānupūrvī booklets, which requires full attention and steadies the mind.

name: Meditation on 'arhaṃ'
method_summary: Meditating on the seed-syllable 'arhaṃ' — visualised shining in the heart or on a lotus, or rising as fire in the fire concentration — as the essence of the Arhat.

name: Recitation of hymns (Bhaktāmara, Uvasaggaharaṃ, Kalyāṇamandira and others)
method_summary: Daily or occasional recitation of hymns to the Jinas, especially the Bhaktāmara (44/48 verses) and the protective Uvasaggaharaṃ to Pārśva; a later tradition attaches a mantra, yantra and benefit to each Bhaktāmara verse.

name: Worship of the Jina's image (pūjā)
method_summary: Bathing the image and offering the eight substances — water, sandal paste, flowers (Digambara: yellow rice), incense, lamp, unbroken rice, sweets and fruit — with hymns; 'material worship' (dravya-pūjā) is a support for 'inner worship' (bhāva-pūjā), the contemplation of the Jina's qualities; the Jina does not respond, the worshipper is purified.
notes: The Sthānakavāsī and Śvetāmbara Terāpanthī traditions reject image worship; the Digambara Terāpantha rejects offerings of flowers and fresh produce and the bhaṭṭārakas' ritual authority (recalled).

name: Worship of the Ṛṣimaṇḍala yantra
method_summary: Recitation of the Ṛṣimaṇḍala hymn and worship of its yantra — the seed 'hrīṃ' surrounded by the syllables of the supreme beings and the twenty-four Jinas — for protection and removal of obstacles.
notes: Restricted: summary only; the mantra is not recorded.

name: Worship of Padmāvatī
method_summary: Worship of the goddess Padmāvatī, attendant of Pārśvanātha, with offerings, mantras and yantras for protection and worldly aims, as set out in the Bhairava-Padmāvatī-kalpa; the practitioner must be devoted to the Jina and the teacher, truthful and self-controlled.

warnings.text: Right view excludes worshipping passionate deities for favours ('folly regarding gods').
Mantra used to harm, attract or subjugate is evil meditation binding karma.

notes: Restricted: summary only (the kalpa includes rites for worldly ends); no mantra, yantra or rite recorded.

name: Practice of the Sūrimantra
method_summary: A Śvetāmbara ācārya, receiving the secret Sūrimantra from his teacher at installation, periodically practises it in its five sections with fasting, silence and worship of the presiding deities; the practice is transmitted orally.
